chapter_title: Concerning the Twelve Signs of the Zodiac and the Five Stars
chapter_note: Extremely high substrate purity. The chapter contains systematic cosmological-correspondential teaching mapping zodiac signs and planets to the five worlds of darkness, then mapping zodiac triplicities to four cosmic domains of affliction. Both mappings stay entirely within the cosmic system — no contemporary application, no institutional content, no exhortation. The editorial layer is limited to dialogue frame formulas (opening/attribution) and first-person recap framing in ¶10-13. The seam flags on ¶3 and ¶10 are false positives — both paragraphs contain pure cosmos→cosmos mappings with zero institutional content. Gardner notes the structural tension of fitting twelve into pentads and reconciling the seven rulers with Mani's system; these tensions are visible in the teaching itself (uneven 2-2-3-3-2 distribution) and represent genuine substratic difficulty, not editorial confusion. The negative editorial fatigue score confirms the substrate runs strong throughout.

paragraphs.core_text: the twelve signs of the zodiac that are set in the sphere. How are they determined? Or to what place do they belong, according to their essence? Or else again, these five stars that circle in them, from whence are they? Or why has the demiurge appointed them as the authorities and leaders? He is the great constructor who has appointed the entire creation; and he has bound and fixed them on the sphere.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formulas: 'Once more, during one of the times, the apostle [is sitting down] ⟨p.167⟩ among the congregation. A disciple stood before him and questioned him. He says to him: We entreat you, our master, that you may recount to us and explain about' (opening frame) and 'Now, we entreat you, our master, that you may satisfy us about these things that are hidden from all mankind.' (closing entreaty)
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological questions define the teaching structure: zodiac distribution, planetary origin, demiurge's role. These are the bones of the Persian pedagogical tradition. The 'demiurge' / 'great constructor' terminology is cosmological, not editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: Whether these twelve signs of the zodiac that are fixed on the sphere, or these five stars that circle upon them; those and these are rulers, all of them, according to their essence. They are all enemies and rivals to each other ⟨one oppresses another, they threaten each other⟩. They plunder one another by the action of the great craftsman who has formed all the worlds. He has gathered [them] and bound them on the sphere above, which circles constantly. Now, while it circles and tumbles them, so they shall do everything that they desire, above and below, according to their pleasure. Nevertheless, a guardian is over them, a debt-collector above them; compelling, extorting, and taking what is theirs away from them!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: 'Then he speaks to that disciple who had questioned him:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological description. The 'guardian' and 'debt-collector' are cosmic agents (the demiurge/Living Spirit), not contemporary officials. The sphere as binding mechanism, plundering among bound rulers, and the overseer extracting from them — all cosmos→cosmos. The ⟨marginal gloss⟩ may be a scribal clarification.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this is how it can rightly be understood. They were [s]eized from the five worlds of Darkness, and bound on the sphere. Two zodiacal signs were taken per world. Gemini and Sagittarius belong to the world of smoke, which is the mind. In contrast, Aries and Leo belong to the world of fire. Taurus, Aquarius and Libra belong to the world of wind. Cancer and Virgo and [P]isces belong to the world of water. Capricorn and Scorpio belong to the world of Darkness. These are the twelve rulers of depravity, the ones that wicked[ness] shall not [ ... ] For they cause all the evil and [ ... in the wo]rld, whether in tree or in flesh.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core correspondential mapping: zodiac signs → five worlds of Darkness. The seam flag is a false positive — 'Now, this is how it can rightly be understood' introduces the systematic mapping, not institutional content. Distribution is uneven (2-2-3-3-2 = 12), reflecting the genuine difficulty of fitting twelve into pentads noted by Gardner. 'World of smoke, which is the mind' — the mind-smoke correspondence is a hallmark of the five-worlds substrate. 'In tree or in flesh' = vegetable and animal kingdoms, cosmic scope.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.168⟩ And understand also about these five stars, the leaders: from where were they formed? The star of Zeus (Jupiter) was generated from the world of smoke, which is the mind. In contrast, Aphrodite (Venus) came about from the world of fire. And then Ares (Mars) belongs to the world of wind. Hermes (Mercury) belongs to the world of water. Cronos (Saturn) belongs to the world [of] Darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second systematic mapping: planets → five worlds of Darkness. One planet per world, clean pentadic structure. The Greek god-names (Zeus, Aphrodite, Ares, Hermes, Cronos) are the Coptic translators' rendering — the substrate likely used Babylonian/Persian planetary names. Jupiter→smoke/mind, Venus→fire, Mars→wind, Mercury→water, Saturn→darkness.

paragraphs.core_text: And also, the two ascendants are counted to fire and desire, the dry and the moist. They are the father and the mother of all these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching about the two lunar nodes (ascending/descending). Maps them to fire and desire, dry and moist, father and mother. These are cosmic polarities. The 'father and mother of all these' designates their generative function in the cosmic system — the nodes as progenitors of the dark powers.

paragraphs.core_text: And also, the sun and the moon, which are counted in with them as a rule ⟨[counte]d to their kind, but why did they count them in with them?⟩ so that they would reign over them. You will discover they subjugate them at every moment.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explains the sun and moon's relationship to the dark powers. The ⟨marginal gloss⟩ preserves what appears to be a scribal question about the tradition. The teaching itself describes a cosmic hierarchy: sun and moon are counted with the dark powers not because they belong to darkness but because they rule over them. Both sides remain within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: These seven we have named, the five stars and the two ascendants: They are the doers of wickedness that do every wicked and bad act in every land, the whole of it, above and below, in every creature, in the dry and the moist, in tree and flesh.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary identifying the seven (5 planets + 2 nodes) and their cosmic scope. 'Above and below, in every creature, in the dry and the moist, in tree and flesh' is cosmic domain language, not contemporary application. The 'dry and moist, tree and flesh' pairs are correspondential categories for mineral-vegetable and animal kingdoms.

paragraphs.core_text: [They] are distributed, appointed on four sides, three per angle in these four places. And they are fixed to this revolving sphere. Aries, Leo and Sagittarius, they three belong to a single side. In contrast, Taurus, Capricorn and Virgo, these other three belong to another side. And then, Gemini, Libra and Aquarius belong to another side. Scorpio, Pisces and Cancer belong to another corner. Now, they are placed like this, appointed to these four parts, and distributed on the sphere.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed first-person dialogue frame: 'Once more I reveal to you about these signs of the zodiac:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second systematic distribution: zodiac signs mapped to four sides/angles of the sphere, three per quadrant. This is the standard astrological triplicities: fire signs (Aries/Leo/Sagittarius), earth signs (Taurus/Capricorn/Virgo), air signs (Gemini/Libra/Aquarius), water signs (Scorpio/Pisces/Cancer). Pure cosmos→cosmos mapping. Note that this four-fold distribution operates on a different axis than the five-fold mapping in ¶3.

paragraphs.core_text: So, when the side of Aries, Leo and Sagittarius will be plundered by the guardian who is over it, who extorts from it and the leaders who move upon it; at that instant shall affliction strike all the four-footed creatures below. However, when [the side] of Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn will be plundered; [affliction] shall ⟨p.169⟩ at once befall the herbs, together with the vegetables and all the fruits of the trees. Yet again, when the side of Scorpio, Pisces and Cancer will be plundered; scarcity shall befall the waters upon the earth, and drought be from place to place. Conversely, should the side of Gemini, Libra and Aquarius be plundered; deformity and stuntedness shall befall the form of mankind from place to place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Magnificent correspondential teaching: each zodiac triplicity maps to a domain of affliction. Fire signs → four-footed creatures (animal kingdom). Earth signs → herbs/vegetables/trees (plant kingdom). Water signs → waters/drought (elemental). Air signs → human form. Both sides stay within the cosmic system — the 'plundering' is a cosmic process, the effects are natural-cosmic categories. The fourfold structure (animal-vegetable-water-human) is a classic correspondential degree system.

paragraphs.core_text: these twelve signs of the zodiac: They were fashioned from the five worlds of Darkness, and bound on the sphere.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed first-person recap frame: 'Behold now, I have explained to you about'. The seam flag is a false positive — no institutional content present, just a recap of substrate teaching.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation of ¶3's teaching. The frame 'Behold now, I have explained to you about' is editorial/dialogue layer recap voice. The cosmological content restates the substrate mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: the other five, the stars: They too came about from the five worlds of the land of Darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed first-person recap frame: 'Also, I have taught you about'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation of ¶4's teaching. Brief substrate restatement: five stars from five worlds of darkness.

paragraphs.core_text: the [t]wo ascendants: They are set to the mystery of fire and desire. They are the dry and the moist, the father and the mother.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed first-person recap frame: 'I have recounted to you also about'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation of ¶5's teaching. Restates the two ascendants' correspondences: fire/desire, dry/moist, father/mother. The 'mystery' language may be a Coptic translation choice for what was originally a more direct cosmological term.

paragraphs.core_text: the sun and the moon: They are strangers to them. Still, because of the constraint of the arrangement, in that the thing receives light, and as they belong and plunder them; because of this they were counted in with them in relation to the calculation of the number. For, the sun and the moon are from out of the greatness, not belonging to the stars and the signs of the zodiac.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed first-person recap frame: 'Again, I have revealed to you about'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extends ¶6's teaching with fuller explanation. Sun and moon are 'from out of the greatness' (light realm) — 'strangers' to the dark powers. They are counted with them only 'because of the constraint of the arrangement' and 'the calculation of the number' (i.e., to make seven and twelve). This is the substrate's own attempt to reconcile the tradition of seven planetary rulers with the doctrine that sun/moon belong to light. Both sides remain within the cosmic system.
